newsitem.title: USA: Helms charges U.S. knew of Cuba shoot-down.
newsitem.headline: Helms charges U.S. knew of Cuba shoot-down.

text.p: Conservative Republican Sen. Jesse Helms charged Thursday the United States knew that three U.S. civilian planes were in danger of being shot down by Cuban MiGs last February and did nothing.
U.S. officials vehemently denied the accusation.

Helms, chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, wrote to Secretary of State Warren Christopher and others saying evidence exists showing that U.S. officials watched on radar as the Cuban fighters headed toward the civilian planes.

The MiGs shot down two of the three planes flown by the Miami-based Cuban-American organisation Brothers to the Rescue. The Feb. 24 attack killed four people, was condemned in Washington and helped lead to tighter U.S. sanctions on the communist-ruled island.

"There is substantial and growing evidence that U.S. military and civilian authorities were aware that three American planes belonging to 'Brothers to the Rescue' were in danger before Cuban fighters shot two of them down in the Florida straits," Helms said in his letter.

A White House official, who asked to remain unidentified, said in recent days a briefing was held in which representatives of various agencies laid out all the evidence they have on the shoot-down and none supported Helms' accusation.
"There is no doubt in my mind whatsoever that the United States took correct and appropriate actions on that day," the official said.

The briefing was held in reaction to similar charges from Representative Dan Burton, a conservative Indiana Republican whose House International Relations Subcommittee held a hearing on the shoot-down last week.

The White House official said officials from the National Security Agency, Central Intelligence Agency, Defence Department, Customs, North American Air Defence Command and the Joint Chiefs of Staff all laid out their evidence to show the accusations are wrong.

"They are utterly false on their face, totally unfounded and the Department of Defence and other departments of the U.S. government have consistently gone out of their way to be totally, completely and absolutely forthcoming in responding to these questions and concerns," the official said.
